class.peasant.family.IND: into a family of ryots who till the land
class.craftsman.IND: from a family of hereditary craftsmen
class.craftsman.family.IND: into a family of hereditary craftsmen
class.trader.family.IND: into a family of bania merchants
class.landowner.family.IND: into the family of a zamindar, lord of villages
class.noble.IND: from a line of rajas and amirs
class.noble.family.IND: into a noble family at court
class.trader.family.gujarat: into a merchant family: the banias and Jains of Gujarat trade across half the world
class.landowner.gujarat: from a line of Rajput landholders
class.landowner.family.gujarat: into a family of Rajput landholders
class.noble.vijayanagara: from a line of nayakas, the raya's war lords
class.noble.family.vijayanagara: into the family of a nayaka, a war lord in the raya's service
prof.farmer.desc.IND: Rice, millet, cotton or sugar cane. A third of the harvest, or even half, goes in tax.
prof.laborer.desc.IND: Carrying bricks on the sultan's building sites, hauling bales at the quay, reaping other men's rice.
prof.artisan.desc.IND: The potter's wheel, the smith's forge or stone carving: the craft is taught from childhood, as it was to your father and grandfather.
prof.weaver.desc.IND: Spinning cotton on the charkha wheel. A fine thread is the weavers' greatest treasure.
prof.midwife.desc.IND: Delivering babies, knowing herbs and charms. You are called to huts and palaces alike.
prof.merchant.desc.IND: Grain, salt, cloth and moneylending. You count in your head faster than a clerk on paper.
prof.sailor.desc.IND: River boats in the delta or ships to Aden and Malacca, depending on the monsoon wind.
prof.soldier.desc.IND: A paik foot soldier, an archer or a horseman serving a sultan, a raja or the raya. Paid, when they pay.
prof.scribe.desc.IND: Keeping accounts, writing letters and deeds in Persian and the local tongue.
prof.physician.desc.IND: Healing by Ayurveda: pulse, herbs, oils, diet. At court there are also hakims who know Greek and Arab medicine.
prof.priest.desc.IND: Reciting hymns, performing rites in the temple and in homes: births, weddings, the funeral pyre.
prof.landholder.desc.IND: Collecting tax from villages, keeping a share and sending the rest up. And answering for it if you fall short.
prof.magistrate.desc.IND: You hold lands and troops in the sovereign's name. A sultan's favour is quickly given and quickly taken away.
prof.matron.as.IND: the mistress of a great house
prof.matron.desc.IND: The women's quarters, the servants, the storerooms, the family weddings: everything rests on you.
prof.household_slave.desc.IND: Serving in the master's house: water, the kitchen, the fan in the heat, errands.
prof.field_slave.desc.IND: Working someone else's field for a debt that never seems to end.
prof.officer.desc.IND: You lead a band of horse and foot, draw pay for all of them and answer for every man.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.IND: Your own looms or kilns, apprentices from your kin, customers from the palace and the bazaar.
prof.shipowner.desc.IND: Your own ship, your own bales of cotton and pepper, and your own risk on every ocean crossing.
prof.official.desc.IND: Serving in the revenue office: measuring fields, lists, seals and endless complaints.
prof.overseer.desc.IND: The master has trusted you with the house, the stores and the other servants.
prof.devadasi.desc: Dedicated to the temple's deity: dance, music and song at rites and festivals. Honoured, yet bound to the temple.
prof.mahout.desc: Raising and driving an elephant: bathing it in the river, feeding it, leading it in processions or into battle. It obeys only you.
prof.muslin_weaver.desc: Weaving Bengal muslin, so fine a whole length slips through a finger ring. Work years ahead for the court and the merchants.
prof.spice_trader.desc: Pepper, ginger, cardamom and cinnamon pass through your hands to Arab and Persian ships. Huge profits, and huge risks.
prof.faqir.desc: Giving up home and property to seek God. You live on alms, walk from shrine to shrine and teach whoever asks.
prof.faqir.desc.islam: A disciple of a Sufi shaykh: prayer, sama singing, service in the khanqah lodge, bread for everyone who comes.
prof.kavi.desc: Composing verse in Persian, Sanskrit or the local tongue. Your patron is generous as long as he likes the poems.
prof.qazi.desc: Judging by the sharia, witnessing marriages and deeds, interpreting the law. Great respect, but no way to please everyone.
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.IND: Rice or roti, dal, vegetables, curds
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.IND: Ghee, fruit, fish, sweets, spices. Good for health
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.IND: Feasts with pilaf, sweets and musicians. Guests remember, the host is praised
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.IND: Wrestling, clubs, exercise on beaten earth. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.IND: A temple, a saint's tomb or a vow to the goddess: prayers and offerings
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.IND: The healer reads your pulse and picks the herbs. Expensive, but fewer deaths
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.IND: A jug of water by the door
lifestyle.baths.sometimes.desc.IND: The river or the temple tank on festival days
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.IND: A morning bath in the river or a stepwell, chatter and news. Must live in a city
focus.health.desc.IND: Bathing, the wrestling ground, rest and herbs
focus.learn.desc.IND: The village pathshala or the mosque maktab: reading and reckoning. The family pays
focus.study.desc.IND: A pandit or a mullah, books, verses by heart. Costs money
focus.religion.desc.IND: Temple or mosque, fasts, vows, pilgrimages
